microarchitecture_summary.implementation_style: Single-clock, register-based ASIC wrapper with a minimal transaction-control datapath and no hidden submodules beyond the explicitly implied control, validation, clamp, and diagnostics functions.
microarchitecture_summary.control_strategy: Sample vehicle_geometry and flow_conditions into internal registers, range-check flow velocity, issue at most one outstanding model_request with a monotonic sequence counter, validate model_response by exact sequence match and freshness, then compute bounded actuator targets from validated response fields using simple deterministic arithmetic or threshold logic.
microarchitecture_summary.state_strategy: All state is synchronous to clk and cleared by the active-high synchronous reset_n; internal state includes sampled inputs, request sequence/outstanding tracking, response age/timeout tracking, live and sticky fault indicators, clamp status, fallback status, and registered actuator outputs.
microarchitecture_summary.output_strategy: Drive all external outputs as registered, glitch-free signals; request outputs reflect the sampled request payload, actuator outputs reflect clamped and optionally rate-limited safe command values, and diagnostics/fault outputs expose live and sticky status derived from the current control state.

fsm_intent.description: A dedicated multi-state FSM is not required by the spec; implement the behavior as simple synchronous state registers with combinational next-state selection for request issue, response acceptance, fault detection, clamp indication, and safe-fallback gating.

internal_storage: Sampled geometry descriptor/payload-handle registers and framing metadata registers.
Sampled flow-condition registers including velocity and metadata.
Monotonic request sequence counter and outstanding-request valid/age tracking.
Captured request payload registers used to drive request_valid, request_id, request_geometry_desc, request_geometry_payload, request_flow_velocity_mps, request_flow_meta, and request_age.
Response validation registers for outstanding request ID, last accepted response ID, response freshness/age, and timeout counting.
Live fault and sticky fault registers for input-range, outstanding-request, response-valid, stale-reject, timeout, clamp-active, and fallback-active conditions.
Registered actuator command hold values and optional rate-limited previous command values for each channel.
output_mapping: request_valid asserts when a sampled request is being presented and the model service can accept it; request_id and request payload fields reflect the registered request snapshot.

safe_fallback_request asserts whenever invalid input, stale response, timeout, malformed response, or interface fault is detected, and remains asserted until a fresh sequence-matched valid response clears the condition.

fault_input_range, fault_request_outstanding, fault_response_valid, fault_stale_reject, fault_timeout, fault_clamp_active, and fault_fallback_active are direct registered indicators of current live fault state.

actuator_command0 and actuator_command1 are registered outputs driven from validated control-law results, then optionally rate-limited, then clamped to min/max limits, otherwise forced to actuator_safe_hold_value during fallback.

diagnostic_live_faults and diagnostic_sticky_faults are packed status views of current and retained fault conditions; diagnostic_request_seq, diagnostic_response_seq, diagnostic_timeout_counter, diagnostic_outstanding, and diagnostic_response_age mirror the internal tracking registers.

sequencing_notes: Sample vehicle_geometry and flow_conditions before any request generation.
Advance the monotonic request_id only when a new request is issued.
Allow only one outstanding request in the baseline implementation; do not launch a new request until the prior one is accepted, rejected, or timed out.
Accept model_response only when model_response_valid is asserted and model_response_id matches the outstanding request_id exactly.
Treat duplicated, stale, out-of-order, malformed, or timed-out responses as rejects that assert fault and fallback behavior.
Update actuator outputs only from validated responses; otherwise hold safe fallback or the last safe registered value as configured.
Clamp and optional rate-limit decisions are performed after the control-law result is formed and before actuator output registration.
timing_notes: All sequential elements update on the rising edge of clk only.
reset_n is implemented as an active-high synchronous reset behavior per spec and clears state on a clock edge.
No combinational feedback loops should be introduced between request generation, response validation, control-law computation, and output registration.
Major datapath decisions should be register-to-register to keep the design ASIC-synthesizable at the stated 50 MHz operating point.
External handshake inputs may be sampled and held internally to decouple the control-plane timing from the external DoMINO service timing.
ownership_notes: The RTL owns request sequencing, input sampling, freshness tracking, response validation, clamp enforcement, diagnostics, and safe-fallback control.
The external DoMINO model service owns model execution only and is not implemented in RTL.
The control law must remain bounded and synthesizable, using simple arithmetic, lookup, or threshold logic only.
Future runtime attachment to NVIDIA-hosted NIM or ChipLoop GPU worker services must not require changes to the safety logic or port definitions.
consistency_notes: Interfaces remain exactly as defined in digital_spec_json.
